**rewind 0.4.0 is on CRAN.** It is the biggest update since the first
release. Most of it came from one question: why does an undo sometimes seem
to do nothing?

[My first post](../2026-08-27-undo-for-shiny/index.qmd) explains what
rewind does. In short, it adds undo and redo to a Shiny app with one call,
`rewind_enable()`. It records the inputs as the user works, and puts them
back at an undo.

## Only what the page can put back

By default, rewind now records only the inputs that the page can put back.

Before 0.4.0, rewind recorded every input of the session. Some inputs have
nothing on the page to put back. The hover of a plot is the clearest case.
`plotOutput(hover = "plot_hover")` sends the position of the pointer as an
input, but no element on the page holds that value.

So each pause of the pointer over the plot became a step. The rail filled
with `plot_hover`, and an undo of such a step changed nothing that the user
could see:

```{=html}
<figure class="post-gif">
<picture>
<source srcset="hover-still.png" media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)">
<img src="hover.gif" width="960" height="540" loading="lazy" alt="A recreated Shiny app with Undo and Redo buttons, a Region select, a history rail and a bar chart whose hover is shown under it. First, with a badge that says rewind 0.3.0, the pointer pauses three times over the bars, and the rail gains three steps called plot_hover. Ctrl+Z moves the rail back one step, and nothing else on the page changes. Then, with a badge that says rewind 0.4.0, the same pointer moves add no step. A change of Region from North to East adds a step called Region, and Ctrl+Z puts North back.">
</picture>
<figcaption>A browser recreation of the same app, first with rewind 0.3.0, then with 0.4.0.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

The same was true of the values that DT keeps, such as `_rows_current`
and `_state`, and of a plot's `click`, `dblclick` and `brush`.

The fix asks the browser. Each input that the page can put back has a Shiny
input binding on an element: a select, a slider, a text box. The browser
now reports which inputs have one, and rewind records only those. Inputs
that are only sent from JavaScript, such as the hover of a plot, have no
binding, so they are left out.

The report arrives after the page has loaded. Until it does, rewind records
every input, as before. That is also what happens in `testServer()`, which
has no browser.

There are two ways to change the default:

- A list in `inputs` is used as it is. Name an input there to record it
  anyway: `rewind_enable(inputs = c("region", "year", "plot_brush"))`.
- `rewind_exclude()` leaves inputs out, from anywhere in the server. More
  on that below.

This is a change of behaviour. An app that relied on the old default to
record a value with no binding now needs to name it in `inputs`. I think
such apps are rare, because an undo of those values did nothing on the
page.

## Why did an undo skip this input?

The new `rewind_status()` answers that in one call. It lists what rewind
records, and gives each other input the reason it is left out:

```r
rewind_status()$captured   # c("region", "year")
rewind_status()$skipped    # c(plot_hover = "cannot be restored by the page",
                           #   pw = "password field")
```

The reasons are `"excluded"`, `"password field"`, `"not in inputs"`,
`"cannot be restored by the page"`, `"action button"`, `"file upload"` and
`"NULL value"`. The list also holds the groups registered with
`rewind_track()`, and the size of the history and the current position.

It depends on the inputs, so it works well in a debug panel:

```r
output$status <- renderPrint(rewind_status())
```

`rewind_exclude()` is the other half. It leaves inputs out of the history,
at any time, and from inside a module:

```r
mod_filters_server <- function(id) {
  moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    rewind_exclude("search")   # the module's own name, not "filters-search"
  })
}
```

It works like `shiny::setBookmarkExclude()`. A second call adds to the
list, and an input that the history already holds is removed from it.

## A view that is not a step

A saved view is a set of input values that the app loads in one go: from a
bookmark, from a list of saved filters, or from the defaults of a user.
Loading a view is not something the user did by hand, so it should not be
a step.

The new `rewind_unrecorded()` runs a block of code whose changes are not a
step:

```r
observeEvent(input$load_view, {
  rewind_unrecorded({
    updateSelectInput(session, "region", selected = "East")
    updateSliderInput(session, "year", value = 2020)
  })
})
```

The changes become part of the current state instead. An undo never goes
back across them:

```{=html}

Ctrl+Z puts 2020 back, and Region stays East: the undo goes back to the loaded view, not to the state before it.">
</picture>
<figcaption>A browser recreation. The app calls rewind_enable(labels = c(region = "Region", year = "Year")), so the rail says "Year".</figcaption>

```

### Why a pause does not work

The help of `rewind_pause()` used to suggest a pause and a resume around
code like this. That does not work, and finding out why was the most
useful part of this release for me.

rewind records in its own observer. That observer depends on every input,
so it runs after the observer that made the change. By then, the resume
has already run. The probe I wrote recorded the change as an ordinary step.

There is a second problem: `update*Input()` sends a message to the browser.
The new value comes back as an input later, after the observer has ended.

So `rewind_unrecorded()` does not pause anything. After the block, it keeps
a short window open, twice the grouping period by default. A change that
arrives in that window replaces the current state, and does not make a new
step. A change from the user that was still waiting becomes its own step
first, so the loaded view never swallows it.

## Names a person reads

The rail and `rewind_diff()` used the input ID as the label of a step. An
ID such as `year` is fine. An ID such as `sel_trt_arm` is not something a
user should read.

`rewind_enable()` now takes `labels`:

```r
rewind_enable(labels = c(region = "Region", trt = "Treatment arm"))
```

The rail shows the labels, and `rewind_diff()` has a new `label` column.
It is the last column, so code that picks the six columns of 0.3.0 by
position still gets the same ones.

## The smaller things

- **Every argument is checked**, with a message that names it. Some wrong
  values used to be accepted, and did the wrong thing with no message:
  `shortcuts = "yes"` turned the shortcuts off, `depth = 2.5` became 2, and
  `rewind_jump(1.9)` moved to position 1.
- **A typo gives a warning.** A name in `inputs` that the page does not
  have, or a name in `rewind_track(fields = )` that the values do not
  have, used to record nothing, with no message.
- **A busy input no longer holds back every step.** The grouping period
  started again whenever any input changed, also an input that is not
  recorded. A plot hover thus held back every step until the pointer
  stopped.
- **Password fields are never kept in the history.** A `passwordInput()`
  sends a plain string, so rewind recorded it like any text box, and
  `rewind_diff()` could show it. The browser now reports which fields are
  passwords, and rewind leaves them out, even when `inputs` names them.
- **`rewind_enable(c("region", "year"))`** put the names into `session`,
  the first argument, and failed with "$ operator is invalid for atomic
  vectors". It now says that `session` must be a Shiny session, and points
  to `inputs = c(...)`.
- **`rewind_example()`** runs the demo app. It replaces
  `shiny::runApp(system.file("examples/demo", package = "rewind"))`.
- **The help of `rewind_track()`** has a new section on environments and
  R6 objects. rewind keeps those by reference, so a change inside such an
  object is not a step, and an undo cannot bring back its old contents.
  The section shows how to change a copy instead.
- **The help of `rewind_enable()`** has a new section on text inputs: why
  slow typing can give several steps, and how
  `textInput(updateOn = "blur")` gives one step for each edit.

## Try it

```r
install.packages("rewind")
rewind::rewind_example()
```

- Documentation: <https://tenmeh.github.io/rewind/>

If an undo in your app still seems to do nothing, call `rewind_status()`
and tell me what it says. That is exactly the kind of case this release
is for.
